title: Section 2
context: A council officer is introducing a city volunteer tree-planting programme to a group of new volunteers.

audio.t: You will hear a council officer talking to new volunteers about a tree-planting programme.
Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming along. I'm delighted to see so many new faces at tonight's welcome session for the Greener Streets programme.
Let me start with a little history. Many people assume the project began as part of a national campaign, but in fact it started after a severe storm six years ago.
That storm brought down more than a thousand trees across the city, and residents were so upset that they asked the council to help them replace them.
Now, a word about when we plant. In the early years we met every Sunday, but too many volunteers told us that Sundays were difficult because of family commitments.
So we changed it, and planting days are now held on the first Saturday of every month, from nine until one.
I know some of you have brought your children along tonight. Children are very welcome, but anyone under sixteen must be accompanied by an adult for the whole session.
It's not enough for a parent to drop them off and come back later, I'm afraid. That's an insurance requirement.
Please wear sensible clothes, because the work does get muddy. We provide gloves and all the tools, so there's no need to bring your own spades.
What we can't provide is footwear. So please wear strong, closed shoes, and ideally waterproof boots if you have them.
As for our targets, the council originally hoped to plant two thousand trees by the end of this decade.
We've been so successful that the goal has been raised to twenty thousand by 2030, which would make this one of the biggest programmes in the region.
Now let me tell you about the five sites we'll be working on this season, and which species goes where.
Our first project is Riverside Park. The soil there is very damp, so we'll be putting in willows, which cope well with wet ground.
Next is Hillcrest School. The head teacher would like the pupils to eat what they grow, so the playground edge will get apple trees.
Then there's Market Square. We first planned to put in oaks, but their roots would damage the old paving stones.
So instead we've chosen maples, which are smaller and also give wonderful colour in autumn.
Along the Canal Path, we'll plant birches. They're slim, so they won't block the towpath, and cyclists will enjoy the shade.
The last site is the Old Quarry. Nothing much grows in that thin, stony ground, but pines are tough enough to survive there.
I should mention that we considered planting some oaks at the quarry too, but we've decided to keep those for a woodland project next year.
Right, if you'd all like to come forward, there are sign-up sheets on the table by the door, and my colleague will hand out the safety leaflets.
Please choose the first Saturday you can attend, and tell us if you have any health conditions we should know about.
Thank you again, and I look forward to seeing you with muddy boots in a few weeks' time.

questions.q: The Greener Streets programme began because
options: the council wanted to attract tourists.
questions.explain: Người nói bác bỏ ý "national campaign" và nói chương trình bắt đầu "after a severe storm" làm đổ hơn một nghìn cây.

options: on the first Sunday of each month.
on the first Saturday of each month.
questions.explain: Lúc đầu họp mỗi Chủ nhật, nhưng đã đổi: "planting days are now held on the first Saturday of every month".

options: stay with an adult throughout the session.
bring a letter from a parent.
work only at the school site.
questions.explain: "anyone under sixteen must be accompanied by an adult for the whole session" - phụ huynh không được chỉ đưa trẻ đến rồi đi.

questions.q: What do volunteers need to bring themselves?
questions.explain: Hội đồng cung cấp găng tay và dụng cụ, nhưng "What we can't provide is footwear", nên phải tự mang giày chắc chắn.

questions.q: What is the new target for the programme?
questions.explain: Mục tiêu ban đầu là hai nghìn cây, nay "raised to twenty thousand by 2030".

questions.explain: Đất rất ẩm nên "we'll be putting in willows" (liễu).
Để học sinh có thể ăn quả: "the playground edge will get apple trees".
Dự định trồng sồi nhưng rễ làm hỏng nền lát, nên "instead we've chosen maples" (phong).
"we'll plant birches. They're slim, so they won't block the towpath".
Đất mỏng nhiều đá nên chọn thông: "pines are tough enough to survive there"; sồi để dành cho dự án năm sau.
